system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback

## 1. Preliminary point: the "pre-categorisation" and "FINAL" labels should be disregarded

Before the substantive review, two framing devices in the Seller's cover note need to be called out:

- The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asks us to treat clauses marked **[STANDARD]** as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to look only at **[OPEN]** items. Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN]; every contentious clause is marked [STANDARD]. There is no record on our side of these positions being cleared, and several of them contradict our playbook's express fallback conditions (e.g. the 20% cap and 18-month period both require Amelia Frost's written authority, which has not been given). The Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] states that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included," which is inconsistent with the cover note's claim that the package was "settled at principal level."
- The "market context" preamble (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months) is advocacy, not an agreed benchmark. We should review against our playbook, not the Seller's description of the market.

**Recommendation:** Respond that we do not accept the [STANDARD]/FINAL categorisation, that no principal-level agreement on the limitation or disclosure package exists on our side, and that all clauses remain open for mark-up.

## 2. Substantive departures from the playbook

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a fallback usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None given.
- **Issue:** The Seller has simply inserted our confidential fallback as the "agreed" position. We cannot accept it without authority.
- **Pushback:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Issue:** Each threshold is five times our position, and the switch to excess-only (deductible) rather than tipping basket is a material economic shift – on a AUD 250,000 basket it effectively forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of every warranty exposure.
- **Pushback:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. Also ensure the de minimis aggregates related claims arising from the same facts.

### 2.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval (none given).
- **Issue:** The 18-month period is again our unauthorised fallback. The second sentence is a hidden general-regime override: unless we expressly carve out every category, the general time bar would catch Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud.
- **Pushback:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with a clause stating that general limitations do **not** apply to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment/covenant claims, or fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** This is one of the most significant departures. Collapsing title into the general regime would mean a defect in ownership of the shares (the entire asset) is capped at 20% and expires at 18 months.
- **Pushback:** Insist on a separate Fundamental Warranty regime: capacity, title, authority, no encumbrances, share capital. 100% of price, 6+ years, no basket, no de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate.
- **Issue:** As drafted there is no fraud carve-out at all, and the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language would purport to bar misleading-conduct claims and specific indemnity claims. Apart from being contrary to the playbook, a blanket purported exclusion of fraud liability is unlikely to be enforceable and signals a poor-faith drafting position.
- **Pushback:** Insert an express, non-waivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause. Confirm specific indemnities, Tax and IP claims and payment/covenant obligations sit outside cl 12 entirely.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** Whole-data-room disclosure shifts the risk of every buried document onto the Buyer. Public-register disclosure is open-ended (undefined searches, unknown dates). Combined with the knowledge bar at cl 8.3, the warranties would be close to meaningless.
- **Pushback:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Require a disclosure standard of "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter." Specific disclosures in sections 2–10 can remain but should be tested individually (see 2.12 below).

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Issue:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar ("discoverable") extended to our advisers – effectively a prudent-search deemed disclosure by another route, and it would gut the Fundamental Warranties and specific indemnities.
- **Pushback:** Delete cl 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it should operate only on the Seller side (warranties given "so far as the Seller is aware," defined by reference to named individuals having made reasonable enquiry), and never on title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; Disclosure Letter [2])
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Issue:** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are met. A consent that is delivered but conditional on unmet conditions would not protect the revenue. "Reasonable endeavours" permits the Seller to fall short with no consequence.
- **Pushback:** Condition precedent = written consent in agreed form, unconditional or with all 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, in force at Completion. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) and to give the Buyer visibility of correspondence. Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment if consent is delayed or conditional.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; Disclosure Letter [3])
- **Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release requires irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Issue:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; security remains in place; change-of-control at 8.1 is presumably triggered by the sale. A post-completion release means the Buyer acquires a company encumbered by its former owner's lender with only a promise of discharge – inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free.
- **Pushback:** Require a Riverlark payout letter dated within a short window before Completion, repayment from the Completion funds directly to Riverlark as a deliverable, and executed releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. Only if genuinely impracticable, accept a lender's irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt, and only with Amelia Frost's approval.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses / funds flow (DD-005; Disclosure Letter [5])
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** The bonuses are payable by the Company on Completion and continued employment, so absent a line item they become a Company (i.e. Buyer-borne) liability post-Completion. The disclosure is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, which could add materially to the AUD 420,000.
- **Pushback:** Either (a) treat the bonuses and all on-costs as Debt / a deduction in the funds flow, or (b) Seller to fund them (with on-costs) before Completion and warrant that they are fully paid or accrued. Request a schedule of on-costs.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; Disclosure Letter [4])
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Issue:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds. If the AUD 180,000 is outstanding, the Company does not own the deliverables. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, infringement exposure, re-development cost or Ironquay claims to the materials.
- **Pushback:** Broaden to an indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of ownership or transfer of SOW3 Project Materials and any Ironquay claim; preserve the right to cure by payment; require Seller to procure payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable, or obtain bank evidence of prior payment. Outside the general caps.

### 2.12 Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; Disclosure Letter [6])
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Issue:** The Seller's characterisation goes beyond what the evidence supports (the Disclosure Letter itself says scope, access and notification status are unknown). Equally, we should not assert a breach has occurred. The risk is that general disclosure of DD-006 would be argued to disclose any later-discovered consequences.
- **Pushback:** Pre-Completion covenant to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide updates and allow Buyer input on any notification decision; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification cost, third-party claims), outside general caps and not defeated by disclosure of DD-006 or any knowledge bar. Do not accept a "not material" characterisation in the SPA.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; Disclosure Letter [8])
- **Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Issue:** Three related AUD 110,000 renewals; the disclosure says nothing about whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Reading DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing is necessary to determine whether they are pre- or post-Completion obligations.
- **Pushback:** Request the renewal terms, notice periods and accrual position. Do not concede ordinary-course characterisation until assessed; reserve the right to treat accrued or non-terminable pre-Completion liabilities as Debt or working-capital items.

### 2.14 Tax / IP
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** remain OPEN; separate categories; assume no resolution.
- **Issue:** Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250,000 regime is a hidden override. Tax exposure in particular commonly runs to the statutory amendment period.
- **Pushback:** Confirm Tax and IP are open and will be addressed in separate schedules with their own caps and periods. (We are not seeking unlimited liability, but the general regime is not appropriate.)

### 2.15 Title evidence (DD-012; Disclosure Letter [10])
- **Seller:** title evidenced by the Company share register.
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is an internal source.
- **Issue:** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes DD-012 is "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. A company's internal register is not independent proof.
- **Pushback:** Obtain ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (relevant to Riverlark security over the shares), Seller constitutional documents and board resolutions, and share certificates; plus Fundamental Warranties on title and no encumbrances under the separate regime (2.4 above).

### 2.16 Other disclosures (lease [7], Mossvale [9])
- Not strictly playbook items, but note: the office lease notification obligation and the Mossvale assignment restriction should be confirmed as non-consent items by our own review of DD-007 and DD-009, not by the Seller's characterisation. Add to Completion deliverables as applicable.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [STANDARD]/FINAL labels | "Cleared by both sides" | Reject; everything is open; no principal agreement exists |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% not authorised |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | 5k / 50k / first-dollar |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + applies to all Claims | 24 months; delete global default |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100%, 6+ years, no basket/knowledge bar |
| 5 | Fraud / all-Claims limitations | No carve-out; applies to everything | Non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete; Seller-side named-person knowledge only |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | Effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, before Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised | Line item incl. on-costs, or Seller-funded |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Broad IP indemnity; SOW3 cure; confirmatory assignment |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Log preservation, investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no characterisation either way |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess terms; no concession yet |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | Open; separate schedules |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/constitutional evidence |

**Priority order for the response:** (i) reject the "cleared" framing and restate that no fallbacks are authorised; (ii) limitation package (cap, thresholds, time, Fundamental regime, fraud carve-out, "all Claims" override); (iii) disclosure and buyer-knowledge; (iv) Completion mechanics (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title evidence); (v) specific risk items (Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar, Tax/IP).

**Internal action:** If the deal team wishes to deploy the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks at any point, obtain Amelia Frost's written authority referencing the specific draft before doing so. Nothing in the Seller's package changes that requirement.
=== END ADVICE ===
